title: store.append acquires a second pool connection while holding the first, exhausting the pool (TC-EXP-301-08)
symptom: TC-EXP-301-08 fails with PoolError.ExhaustedPool raised at src/db/pool.zig:783 (`if (self.idle_count == 0) return PoolError.ExhaustedPool`), reached from src/event_store/store.zig:428 (`const dup_conn = self.pool.acquire() catch return StoreError.PoolExhausted;`), called from the test's second `store.append(allocator, params)` at tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig:886.
root_cause_analysis: On the duplicate-idempotency-key path, store.append acquires a SECOND connection from the pool to look up the original event while its first connection is still held for the in-flight transaction. Under parallel test execution the pool has no idle connection left to hand out, so the nested acquire fails. This is a connection-discipline defect in production code, not a test-fixture problem: any caller that appends a duplicate event while the pool is saturated hits it. It is self-deadlock-shaped — the same call path holds and then demands a second lease from a finite pool.
impact: 1 of the 3 remaining effects_subsystem_test failures. In production this surfaces as spurious StoreError.PoolExhausted on idempotent re-appends under load, i.e. exactly when a retry storm is in progress and dedup matters most.
acceptance_criteria: The duplicate-lookup path no longer acquires a second pool connection while the first is held — reuse the connection already in hand, or perform the lookup after releasing it
TC-EXP-301-08 passes under a loaded parallel run
A regression test covers append-of-duplicate while the pool has zero idle connections
No other store.zig path nests pool.acquire() inside a held lease
related: ISS-0158 / GH #479 -- the run that isolated this as a distinct cause
ISS-0132 / GH #427 -- the leak-class closure whose allocation-failure discipline pattern this run follows
notes: Filed per CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only' and the 'filed and forwarded, not fixed here' scope boundary. Unrelated to the SERVICE_TASK effect-emission ownership defects fixed under ISS-0158. Resolved under WF03-GH521-20260808 (own branch, own PR, own merge); no scope bleed into ISS-0158's branch.
resolution: Removed the nested self.pool.acquire() at the duplicate-idempotency-key path in src/event_store/store.zig (was 3 lines: const dup_conn = self.pool.acquire() catch return StoreError.PoolExhausted; defer self.pool.release(dup_conn);). Both duplicate-lookup queries (events table, events_archive) now reuse the held, ROLLBACK'd conn from the outer transaction -- by the time the duplicate-detection branch executes, line 435 has issued ROLLBACK, so the conn is no longer in any transaction and is safe to issue read-only SELECTs against. StoreError.PoolExhausted remains a variant but is now reachable only at the 6 legitimate single-acquire sites (lines 277, 559, 666, 724, 895, 955). Net diff: +12/-4 lines in src/event_store/store.zig. No migration required (code-only). New regression test TC-EXP-202-05 (Pool-size-3 duplicate append) at tests/integration/entity_subsystem_test.zig forces pool_size=3 and runs 3 concurrent createRecord calls with the same idempotency key. Verification: zig build test-integration-exp = 13/13 PASS on 5 consecutive runs; Step 6 revalidation = 13/13 PASS (1s MaxRSS:12M, 0 orphaned tenants); zig build = 0; zig build bench overall_passed=true with all 5 measured NFRs passing (NFR-01 p99_read 1.326ms vs 200ms; NFR-01 p99_write 9.917ms vs 500ms; NFR-02 throughput 13932 ev/s vs 1000; NFR-04 replay_10000 37.799ms vs 5000; NFR-04 replay_snapshot_100000 5.248ms vs 1000); tools/lint_test_isolation.py = 0 BLOCKER; tools/lint_sql_param_types.py = 0 BLOCKER/MAJOR; tools/lint_design_artefact.py = 0; tools/verify_test_env.py = 10/10 PASS.
